item.title: China says U.S. has no say on selection of BBNJ Secretariat seat
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
China says U.S. has no say on selection of BBNJ Secretariat seat BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese spokesperson said on Wednesday that the United States, which is neither a state party to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea nor to the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, has no say on the selection of the BBNJ Secretariat seat. Guo Jiakun, the spokesperson for the Chinese foreign ministry, made the remarks when asked to comment on a statement issued by the U.S. State Department welcoming the joint bid by Chile and Belgium to host the Secretariat of the BBNJ Agreement. "We call on all parties to stay vigilant against attempts to politicize the bidding and create confrontation in the process," said Guo. He stressed that China has made clear its position on the Belgium-Chile proposal, adding that this joint candidature is problematic in at least six aspects, namely, it contravenes the stipulations of the BBNJ Agreement, procedural justice, established international practice, equitable geographical distribution, fair competition and the original commitment. "According to the BBNJ Agreement, the seat of the Secretariat, the specific modalities for the operation of the Clearing-House Mechanism (CHM), including its installation, as well as where the subsidiary bodies hold their meetings shall all be determined by the Conference of the Parties, and the CHM shall be managed by the Secretariat," said Guo. These are the consensus as well as rights and responsibilities of all Parties to the Agreement, which no country has the right or is in any position to violate, he added. "No one shall trade under the table what should be collectively determined by all Parties, let alone coerce or hijack other Parties into accepting their proposal," Guo noted. As one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China stands ready to work with the international community to uphold the original purpose of the Agreement and keep the selection of the Secretariat seat proceeding in the right direction, so that the BBNJ Agreement can truly serve the shared interests of humanity, said Guo. item.title: China urges Japan to accelerate destruction of abandoned chemical weapons
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
China urges Japan to accelerate destruction of abandoned chemical weapons This photo taken on Nov. 25, 2026 shows the scene of a side event hosted by the Chinese delegation at the 31st Session of the Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CSP-31) in The Hague, the Netherlands. China urged Japan to accelerate the destruction of abandoned chemical weapons in China at the CSP-31 in The Hague on Wednesday, stressing that prolonged delays in addressing the issue remain a major practical obstacle to achieving "a world free of chemical weapons." (Xinhua/Shao Haijun) THE HAGUE, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China urged Japan to accelerate the destruction of abandoned chemical weapons in China at the 31st Session of the Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CSP-31) in The Hague on Wednesday, stressing that prolonged delays in addressing the issue remain a major practical obstacle to achieving "a world free of chemical weapons." The Chinese delegation hosted a side event titled "Current Status and Challenges with Respect to the Destruction of the Chemical Weapons Abandoned by Japan on the Territory of China," highlighting delays in the destruction process and calling on Japan to fulfill its obligations under the Convention. More than 100 representatives from over 40 countries attended the event. According to the Chinese delegation, Japan has missed its deadlines for destroying the abandoned chemical weapons four times. The latest plan, adopted in 2022, is due to expire in 2027, putting Japan at risk of missing the deadline for a fifth time. Japan's budget for addressing the abandoned chemical weapons in China was cut by 22 percent this year compared with 2025, even as its defense budget continued to rise. Shen Bo of China's Permanent Representation to the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) said discussions at the Conference of the States Parties had reflected several shared understandings within the international community regarding the Japanese abandoned chemical weapons. "Concerns are growing over delays in the destruction process, particularly the risk that Japan could miss the 2027 deadline. The international community expects Japan, as the state that abandoned the weapons, to fulfill its obligations under the Convention and accelerate their destruction," Shen said. He said Japan must adopt a serious and responsible attitude toward its historical, political and legal responsibilities. Any attempt to whitewash its wartime crimes or rewrite history would not be accepted by China or the international community. "Japan must show genuine commitment by faithfully fulfilling its obligations under the Convention and substantially increasing investment in personnel, technology and funding. It must also take swift action by providing accurate information on burial sites, improving the efficiency of excavation and recovery operations, and assuming responsibility for treating contaminated soil and water," Shen told Xinhua after the side event. Vladimir Tarabrin of the Permanent Representation of the Russian Federation to the OPCW said Russia's position on the chemical weapons abandoned by Japan during World War II was "clear and unequivocal." "This is not a matter of Japan's goodwill, nor is it an act of charity. It is Japan's legal and moral obligation to rid itself of this legacy of the Second World War as soon as possible," he added. OPCW Director-General Sabrina Dallafior stressed that recovering and destroying the chemical weapons abandoned by Japan in China is an important part of the international community's shared goal of permanently and completely eliminating chemical weapons worldwide. "This is a difficult task, but one that must be accomplished," she said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi says joint space exploration by Chinese, Pakistani astronauts vivid embodiment of deep-rooted friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
Xi says joint space exploration by Chinese, Pakistani astronauts vivid embodiment of deep-rooted friendship BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the joint space exploration by astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries. It marks another important achievement in bilateral cooperation, Xi said while exchanging congratulations with Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari on the joint spaceflight mission. In the message, Xi said that he was glad to learn of a Pakistani astronaut's successful entry into space aboard a Chinese Shenzhou spaceship for the first time, making him the first foreign astronaut to inhabit China's space station. Xi extended his warm congratulations to the Pakistani government and people, as well as to astronauts and space professionals from both countries on behalf of the Chinese government and people. Xi noted that China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners, saying that the friendship between the two countries has remained rock-solid and unbreakable since diplomatic ties were established 75 years ago. Emphasizing that China's space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation, Xi said that China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to advance the peaceful use of outer space, deepen international space cooperation, and improve global governance in outer space, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity. For his part, Zardari expressed profound appreciation to the Chinese government and the brotherly Chinese people on behalf of the Pakistani government and people. He said the historic space cooperation between Pakistan and China and the first Pakistani astronaut entering China's space station come as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. Such cooperation demonstrates China's remarkable progress in space science and technology, its firm commitment to the peaceful use of outer space, and the significance of building a community with a shared future for humanity, Zardari said, adding that it will further strengthen bilateral friendship, and promote the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries to a higher level. item.title: The intelligent economy: A new engine for China's development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
The intelligent economy: A new engine for China's development Staff members use a hexapod robot for intelligent inspection operations at a substation in Lai'an county, Chuzhou, east China's Anhui province. (Photo/Lyu Hua) Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping economic and social development at an unprecedented pace and scale, yielding profound and far-reaching impacts. A newly released Chinese large language model draws developers from around the world; smart vehicles travel along urban roads; robotic arms work with precision on factory floors; and driverless mining trucks move through underground mines. A new form of the economy, driven primarily by AI and encompassing a wide range of activities in production, distribution and application, is taking shape at an accelerating speed. In recent years, China's intelligent economy has expanded rapidly, improved significantly in quality and continued to optimize its structure. A robotic arm manufactures high-performance carbon fiber raw materials in a smart workshop of a new materials enterprise in Rongcheng, east China's Shandong province. (Photo/Li Xinjun) On one side, the intelligent economy drives the industrialization of AI, turning advances in AI technology into industrial applications and building a growing core AI industry. On the other, it promotes the intelligent transformation of industries, using the "AI Plus" initiative to bring AI applications into the real economy and drive its transformation and upgrading. The intelligent economy is a towering structure, while algorithms, computing power, data and energy form its foundation. Only with a solid foundation can the intelligent economy grow and thrive. Today, China's domestic large AI models are advancing rapidly in a competitive race, with homegrown foundation models ranking among the world's leading offerings. China is helping lead the development of the global open-source AI ecosystem, and Chinese open-source models rank first worldwide in download volume. The country's total intelligent computing capacity ranks second globally, while computing clusters with over 10,000 accelerators are being deployed at an accelerating rate. China's data resources system is becoming more robust, with 120,000 high-quality datasets already established. The country's energy infrastructure provides ample supply: China generates about 1/3 of the world's electricity and has built the world's largest and fastest-growing renewable energy system. Deeper coordination between computing infrastructure and power supply is enabling a steady flow of green electricity, giving China an important advantage in AI development. China's AI industry has maintained annual growth of more than 20 percent for consecutive years, building a comprehensive industrial ecosystem spanning foundational resources, technologies and models, and industry applications. The value of the intelligent economy lies not only in creating new industries, but also in transforming existing ones. While AI first gained widespread adoption in areas such as the internet, it is now rapidly becoming integrated into key production processes across traditional industries. Intelligent upgrades are enabling large amounts of previously underused production capacity to meet overseas demand for customized products at scale and with greater efficiency. AI cuts power grid dispatch cycles from hours down to minutes, helping tackle the problem of renewable energy consumption amid massive grid integration. At unmanned ports, massive cargo ships can start operations immediately upon berthing, and cargo gets transferred right after arrival. This embeds "China efficiency" into key global shipping hubs. Historical evidence shows that breakthroughs in technological capability consistently create new pathways for economic expansion. The next phase of AI industrialization holds substantial promise. AI agents are evolving from content generation tools into autonomous task executors, while humanoid robotics are advancing from demonstration stages to practical industrial deployment. By combining China's vast market demand and diverse application scenarios with its strong manufacturing capabilities and varied business models, the country can foster a wider range of industrial applications and nurture more world-class companies. By the end of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the size of industries related to AI is expected to exceed 10 trillion yuan ($1.49 trillion). An engineer trains a robot to perform tasks in different scenarios at an embodied AI data collection and training base in Huzhou, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/Yao Haixiang) The potential for intelligent transformation across industries is equally significant, with upgrades offering scope for growth many times over. China's manufacturing sector has ranked first globally in overall scale for 16 consecutive years. Every one-percentage-point increase in the adoption of AI across manufacturing would bring thousands of industrial enterprises above the designated size into the ranks of intelligent production. Smart cars, smart homes and other applications will also unlock new sources of growth. According to a policy paper released by the State Council on thoroughly implementing the "AI Plus" initiative, by 2030 AI will comprehensively support high-quality development in China, with adoption rates for next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents exceeding 90 percent. The intelligent economy will become a major growth driver for China's economy. The outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan calls for the comprehensive implementation of the "AI Plus" initiative and stresses the need to seize the commanding heights of AI applications in industry and empower industries across the board. To develop the intelligent economy, China will pursue a coordinated approach that combines targeted breakthroughs, stronger links across the system and broad-based application. At the level of individual technologies, China will focus on key areas and make breakthroughs in critical core technologies. At the level of industrial coordination, it will strengthen synergies among essential factors of production and establish a robust system of production factors suited to the needs of the intelligent economy. At the level of broad-based application, it will tap into ubiquitous real-world scenarios and leverage the advantages of China's enormous market to accelerate the deployment of AI solutions. By strengthening technological capabilities, the supporting ecosystem and real-world applications in an integrated manner, China will continue to expand, improve and strengthen its intelligent economy. item.title: What does "China Haul" reveal about China?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
What does "China Haul" reveal about China? Foreign visitors learn about a pocket-sized gimbal camera at a retail store of Chinese drone maker DJI in Pudong New Area, east China's Shanghai. (Photo/Wang Chu) A trend known as "China Haul" has recently been gaining momentum across global social media platforms. Foreign social media users have been enthusiastically sharing their shopping experiences in China, with many saying they plan to bring larger or additional suitcases on their next trips, while others mention that they buy novel products every time they vacation in China. Smart products made in China, from children's smartwatches to virtual reality (VR) headsets, have become popular topics of discussion. As online buzz continues to grow, visitor numbers are also on the rise. The latest figures from China's National Immigration Administration show that China recorded more than 11.6 million inbound visits by foreign nationals in the third quarter this year, up 15.6 percent year on year. Of these, over 8.99 million were visa-free entries, accounting for 77.5 percent of the total, a year-on-year increase of 24.1 percent. Behind the "China Haul" phenomenon lies a deeper shift in how the world views Chinese products. Technology wins hearts through innovation Foreign influencers' unboxing lists feature not only Guochao (China chic) garments and accessories from Chinese sportswear brands such as Li-Ning and Anta, but also what have become popular Chinese tech specialties, including DJI drones, Insta360 action cameras, and Huawei foldable smartphones. Immersive experiences with cutting-edge technology are also emerging as a new draw for inbound tourists. At a 3D-printing flagship store in Nanshan district, Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province, visitors can scan a QR code to start a personalized 3D-printing experience. In Huaqiangbei, a major electronics hub in Shenzhen, they can browse an array of advanced products, including artificial intelligence (AI)-powered glasses and companion robots. Tours of smart factories, meanwhile, are becoming increasingly popular, giving visitors a close-up look at China's advanced manufacturing capabilities. The growing popularity of Chinese tech products reflects foreign visitors' growing recognition of China's innovation capabilities. Insta360, a Chinese camera and imaging technology company headquartered in Shenzhen, has shipped more than 10 million cameras worldwide. Its first flagship store in New York City attracted more than 1,000 visitors on its first day of operation. Chinese drone maker DJI has long maintained a leading position in the global consumer drone market with a market share of more than 70 percent, and continues to dominate major markets in North America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region. Chinese tech giant Huawei's foldable smartphones have recorded cumulative global shipments of more than 20 million units, reflecting their continuously growing market acceptance. Boasting technological prowess and rapid innovation, Chinese brands are reshaping long-held perceptions among consumers worldwide. A foreign visitor tries out a stringless guitar at Yingyueli Block in Huishan Ancient Town, Wuxi, east China's Jiangsu province. (Photo/Pan Zhengguang) Chinese aesthetics strike a chord White Rabbit, a household Chinese candy brand, has unexpectedly become a hit overseas, garnering more than 6 million views on social media. Its signature red, blue, and white color scheme, together with its clean, crisp lines and patterns, gives the small candy wrapper a distinctive visual identity. It embodies the understated elegance of Chinese aesthetics while offering an instantly recognizable design. Many foreign internet users have hailed it as a "masterpiece of graphic design," sharing it voluntarily and even creating their own interpretations. The White Rabbit-themed store on Nanjing Road in east China's Shanghai has also become a popular tourist destination, with foreign visitors accounting for as much as 30 percent of orders during peak seasons. Behind this growing fascination with Chinese aesthetics is a profound shift in how foreign visitors approach China: they are increasingly experiencing the country with an open mind, free of prejudice and preconceived notions. From historic sites and intangible cultural heritage to popular snacks and trendy cultural and creative products, everyday consumer goods are becoming vibrant carriers for Chinese culture today, turning the country's rich heritage into everyday experiences that people can touch, collect, and taste. Chinese aesthetics, blending traditional charm with modern creativity, are winning an increasingly enthusiastic global following. Foreign visitors shop for cultural and creative souvenirs at a store in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi province. (Photo/Zhang Cheng) Convenient services encourage visitors to stay and shop The growing enthusiasm among foreign visitors for shopping in China is underpinned by concrete policy measures that make travel and consumption easier. China has granted unilateral visa-free entry to nationals of 50 countries and implemented a 240-hour visa-free transit policy for nationals of 57 countries. The latter covers 65 designated ports of entry across 24 provincial-level regions. Such favorable policies are making spontaneous trips to China more accessible than ever. The consumer experience has also continued to improve. China's departure tax refund policy 2.0 has taken effect, with instant tax refund services being rolled out nationwide. The allowable departure period for instant tax refunds has been extended to 28 days nationwide, making it easier for visitors to shop in one place and leave the country from another. The rising share of visa-free entries, coupled with increasing convenience in border clearance and shopping services, is making China an increasingly attractive destination where foreign visitors are willing to visit, stay longer, and spend more. Arriving with empty suitcases and leaving with them full, visitors unpack their bags, revealing a China that combines technological prowess, rich aesthetic traditions, and a genuine commitment to openness, while also showing the world a real China that is modern, lively, and full of the vitality of everyday life. item.title: Xi urges advancing building of Party regulations, institutions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Xi urges advancing building of Party regulations, institutions BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged continuous and high-quality advancement in the building of regulations and institutions of the Communist Party of China (CPC), and upholding rule-based governance as the basic approach to governing the Party. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on the work related to Party regulations and institutions. Xi said the CPC has made solid efforts and achieved notable achievements in strengthening Party regulations and institutions over the past five years. To provide institutional guarantees for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance and ensuring the Party remains the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics, Xi urged enhanced efforts in the systematic integration, education and enforcement of Party institutions, as well as in improving the alignment and coordination of Party rules and regulations with state laws and regulations. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national meeting on the work related to Party regulations held in Beijing on Tuesday and Wednesday. Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the meeting. Running the Party through institutions and regulations is one of the core meanings of Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Cai noted, calling for efforts to enhance the level of running the Party through regulations across the board.
